findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes every reminder type, not just SMS
findings.body: The new deleteMany OR branch matches retryCount > 1 with no method (or scheduled) filter. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP, and this cron now deletes any of those rows once retryCount exceeds 1, including future reminders that were never part of this SMS job. That drops unrelated workflow reminders and, if a row was already handed to a provider, removes the only referenceId needed to cancel it. Scope the clause to unscheduled SMS reminders (method SMS and scheduled false), matching the comment and the PR intent.

findings.title: Unsendable SMS reminders never increment retryCount
findings.body: retryCount is only increased when twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws. If sendTo is missing or the message is empty, the if block is skipped and the row stays scheduled: false with retryCount 0. The cron will keep selecting that reminder on every run until scheduledDate is in the past, which is the infinite reschedule this PR is meant to stop (for example a booking with no attendee phone number). Count that path as a failed attempt, or delete it, so it cannot spin until the event date.

findings.title: Catch treats a successful Twilio schedule as a failed retry
findings.body: The new retryCount update sits in a catch that wraps both twilio.scheduleSMS and the following prisma update that stores scheduled and referenceId. If the provider accepts the message and the DB update then fails, the catch increments retryCount, leaves scheduled false, and never saves the SID. The next cron schedules a duplicate SMS, and after two such failures the opening deleteMany removes the row while Twilio still has the message queued and there is no referenceId left to cancel it. Only increment retryCount when scheduleSMS itself fails, and do not count a post-success persistence error as an exhausted attempt.

findings.title: retryCount increment is a lost update
findings.body: Both failure paths write retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 from the value read at the start of the run instead of an atomic increment. Overlapping cron invocations can each read the same count, each call Twilio, and each write the same next value, so the gt: 1 deletion never trips and duplicate SMS can be scheduled. Use Prisma's increment so concurrent failures cannot collapse to one count.
